note: Synthetic hit-time fixtures for drum benchmark and fast-roll stress tests (issues #121, #123). Raw audio/video is never committed; only expected and detected hit timestamps.

clips.note: 16th notes at 200 bpm = 75 ms between strokes, comfortably above minimumSeparationMs. Kept as the baseline roll; it does not reach the ceiling, which is why fast-roll-32nd exists.

32nd notes at 220 bpm = 34.1 ms between strokes on one zone, below the 35 ms minimumSeparationMs and below every per-zone cooldown in use. This is the clip that actually stresses the roll path (#123); the declared clip set already asked for 180-220 bpm, so the upper bound of that range was unreachable under the previous scoring rule.

One real stroke plus a spurious re-trigger 11 ms later with no intervening lift. The extra detection matches no expected hit, so it must still be counted as a false double: roll tolerance must not become double-trigger blindness (backlog 061).
Sticks rest inside the snare zone; no downstroke, so no hits expected.
